gen-silkscreen-zilla-slab: Pixel-grid retro, with room around every letter that Silkscreen draws like a technical pen. Zilla Slab is the sturdier voice, a slab-serif with broad, open curves.
gen-special-elite-fs-chillax: Special Elite hits the page with a distressed, typewriter-worn look and an x-height that fills the line, while Chillax loosens things up. Its relaxed sans curves stay softer and lower.
gen-special-elite-fs-plein: Special Elite is scruffy and distressed, its tall lowercase and wide-mouthed a grabbing attention right away. Plein is the plain sans that follows, clean and reliable, happy to let the heading make the noise.
gen-special-elite-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans reads as approachable and modern, with wide gaps in its curves. Special Elite's tall, worn lowercase then adds grit that the uniform strokes below keep in check.
gen-special-elite-fs-synonym: Synonym brings a dependable, clean stripe of ink with generous openings in every curve. And Special Elite above it supplies the distressed, tall-lowercase attitude that the sans-serif never tries for.
gen-special-elite-plus-jakarta-sans: Distressed and a bit rebellious, Special Elite fills the line with its tall lowercase and wide-mouthed a. And Plus Jakarta Sans answers with modern, monoline precision, so a modest body size lets it stay quietly in the background.
gen-special-elite-sora: Special Elite's lowercase fills the line to the top. Sora follows with a plain sans feel, geometric and pipe-cleaner thin, so paragraphs move along smoothly with wide, unpinched curves.
gen-special-elite-space-grotesk: Space Grotesk has counters that breathe and a ribbon of constant width, a geometric sans that stays out of the way of Special Elite's worn, tall letters. Paragraphs move along steadily.
gen-syne-gf-courier-prime: Syne takes the lead with experimental, commanding curves that never pinch and a lowercase rising close to cap height. Courier Prime follows in its monospace rhythm, precise and drafting-pen steady across a long page.
gen-syne-gf-fragment-mono: Syne is commanding and strange, its smooth curves rising nearly to cap height. But Fragment Mono lays its monospace letters out like nails on a ruler, so a long passage ticks along without thick-and-thin contrast slowing the eye.
